newsitem.title: NORWAY: Saga's Snorre, Tordis pumped 100 mln bls in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Saga's Snorre, Tordis pumped 100 mln bls in 1996.

text.p: Saga Petroleum ASA said on Monday production at the Norwegian North Sea Snorre and Tordis fields amounted 100 million barrels of oil in 1996.
The Snorre platform flowed 72.4 million barrels, while Tordis yielded 28.6 million barrels.

Average output at Snorre was 198,400 barrels per day (bpd) over the 12-month period. By the end of the year the field was producing from 14 platform and seven subsea wells, Saga said in its weekly newsletter.

"I'm particularly pleased with this Snorre result because we've hit our production target while producing, drilling and working over wells simultaneously," said Hans Morten Stroemmevold, production vice president in Saga's operations division.

"We've also completed Vigdis module installation and debottlenecking of production capacity on Snorre...When production capacity was tested before Christmas, we set a new record of 250,000 barrels of oil."
The Vigdis prospect is due to come on stream in the first half of 1997 and will produce via subsea installation tied back to Snorre.
Tordis pumped an average 77,5000 bpd in 1996, and was producing from five wells by the end of the year.
Saga said it had upgraded capacity at Gullfaks C, through which Tordis oil is piped, to 100,000 bpd from 87,500 bpd.
"A slowly-rising water cut is steadily reducing the volume of oil, which can only be offset by securing pure oil from new wells. Tordis East should provide a boost in 1997," Stroemmevold said.
